classification.difficultyReason: Translate differently oriented congruent rectangles into length-and-width equations; the hardest part requires recognising that the 19 cm arrow measures a difference of stack heights before solving.

content.prompt: What are the lengths and widths of the congruent rectangles for each question?

spec.description: Two alternating stacks, aligned at their lower ends. Left: four horizontal and three vertical rectangles. Right: two horizontal and one vertical rectangle. Each arrow spans its complete stack.
spec.mathematics: 3L+4W=33; L+2W=13. Rectangles are congruent; drawing proportions are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 33 cm and 13 cm measurements are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ and $W$ be the length and width in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}3L+4W&=33 &&\text{(1)}\\L+2W&=13 &&\text{(2)}\\2L+4W&=26 &&\text{(2)}\times2\end{align*}$$
Subtract the last equation from (1).
$$\begin{align*}L&=7\\7+2W&=13\\2W&=6\\W&=3\end{align*}$$
The length is $7\text{ cm}$ and the width is $3\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Two alternating stacks, aligned at their lower ends. Left: five horizontal and four vertical rectangles. Right: four horizontal and three vertical rectangles. Each arrow spans its complete stack.
spec.mathematics: 4L+5W=30; 3L+4W=23. Rectangles are congruent; drawing proportions are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 30 cm and 23 cm measurements are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ and $W$ be the length and width in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}4L+5W&=30 &&\text{(1)}\\3L+4W&=23 &&\text{(2)}\\16L+20W&=120 &&\text{(1)}\times4\\15L+20W&=115 &&\text{(2)}\times5\end{align*}$$
Subtract the last equation from the preceding equation.
$$\begin{align*}L&=5\\3(5)+4W&=23\\4W&=8\\W&=2\end{align*}$$
The length is $5\text{ cm}$ and the width is $2\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Left stack has five vertical rectangles above three horizontal rectangles. Right stack has three vertical rectangles above two horizontal rectangles. Lower ends align, and measurement arrows span the full heights.
spec.mathematics: 5L+3W=23; 3L+2W=14. Rectangles are congruent; drawing proportions are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 23 cm and 14 cm measurements are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ and $W$ be the length and width in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}5L+3W&=23 &&\text{(1)}\\3L+2W&=14 &&\text{(2)}\\10L+6W&=46 &&\text{(1)}\times2\\9L+6W&=42 &&\text{(2)}\times3\end{align*}$$
Subtract the last equation from the preceding equation.
$$\begin{align*}L&=4\\3(4)+2W&=14\\2W&=2\\W&=1\end{align*}$$
The length is $4\text{ cm}$ and the width is $1\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Left: three vertical rectangles stacked beside two horizontal rectangles sharing the bottom baseline. The 19 cm arrow runs from the top of the horizontal pair to the top of the vertical stack. Right: one vertical rectangle above three horizontal rectangles, with a full-height 21 cm arrow.
spec.mathematics: 3L-2W=19; L+3W=21. The 19 cm measurement is a height difference. Rectangles are congruent; drawing proportions are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 19 cm and 21 cm measurements are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ and $W$ be the length and width in centimetres. The $19\text{ cm}$ measurement is the difference between the two heights.
$$\begin{align*}3L-2W&=19 &&\text{(1)}\\L+3W&=21 &&\text{(2)}\\3L+9W&=63 &&\text{(2)}\times3\end{align*}$$
Subtract (1) from the last equation.
$$\begin{align*}11W&=44\\W&=4\\L+3(4)&=21\\L&=9\end{align*}$$
The length is $9\text{ cm}$ and the width is $4\text{ cm}$.
